name: St. John Chrysostom
title: Archbishop of Constantinople
bio: Renowned preacher and Archbishop of Constantinople, celebrated for his eloquence and his liturgy still used in the Orthodox Church today.

name: St. George
title: Great Martyr
bio: A Roman soldier martyred for his Christian faith, venerated across the Orthodox world as a symbol of courage and the slayer of the dragon.

name: St. Mary of Egypt
title: Venerable
bio: A former sinner who repented and lived decades alone in the desert beyond the Jordan, becoming a model of repentance and asceticism.

locations.label: Desert of repentance — beyond the Jordan

name: St. Gregory Palamas
title: Archbishop of Thessalonica
bio: A monk of Mount Athos and later Archbishop of Thessalonica, he defended the hesychast practice of contemplative prayer against the rationalist Barlaam of Calabria, teaching that God's uncreated energies can truly be experienced by the faithful.

name: St. Nectarios of Aegina
title: Metropolitan of Pentapolis, Wonderworker
bio: Born Anastasios Cephalas, he served as Metropolitan of Pentapolis before being unjustly removed from his post; he later founded Holy Trinity Monastery on Aegina, where he spent his final years and is remembered for many posthumous healing miracles.

name: St. Spyridon of Trimythous
title: Bishop, Wonderworker
bio: A simple Cypriot shepherd who became Bishop of Trimythous and attended the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, where he famously explained the Holy Trinity using a piece of brick; his incorrupt relics are now venerated in Corfu, of which he is patron saint.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Trimythous, Cyprus

name: St. Dionysios of Zakynthos
title: Archbishop, Venerable
bio: Born Draganigos Sigouros, he became a monk and later Archbishop of Aegina before retiring to a monastery on his native Zakynthos; he is remembered above all for forgiving the man who, unknowingly, had killed his own brother.

locations.label: Birthplace, monastic life, and relics — Zakynthos

name: St. Cosmas of Aetolia
title: Hieromartyr, Equal-to-the-Apostles
bio: A monk of Mount Athos who spent 25 years traveling on foot throughout Greece and Albania, founding over 200 schools and preaching to villagers left without churches or priests after centuries of Ottoman rule, before being martyred on charges brought against him.

name: St. Basil the Great
title: Archbishop of Caesarea, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs
bio: Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia and a leading 4th-century theologian, he defended Orthodoxy against Arianism and founded the Basiliad, a combined poorhouse, hospital, and hostel for the destitute outside his city.

locations.label: Birthplace, episcopal see, and death — Caesarea, Cappadocia

name: St. Gregory the Theologian
title: Archbishop of Constantinople, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs
bio: A close friend of St. Basil the Great, he was chosen Archbishop of Constantinople by the Second Ecumenical Council for his defense of the Trinity against Arianism, before retiring to Nazianzus for the rest of his life.

name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
title: Great Martyr
bio: A learned and noble young woman of Alexandria who confounded fifty pagan philosophers sent to refute her Christian faith and was martyred under Emperor Maximinus; her relics were later found at the monastery bearing her name on Mount Sinai.

name: St. Panteleimon
title: Great Martyr, Unmercenary Healer
bio: A physician of Nicomedia who treated the poor and sick without charge in the name of Christ, he was martyred under Emperor Maximian after healing a paralyzed man before the emperor's own eyes; he is invoked among the unmercenary healer-saints.

name: St. Anthony the Great
title: Venerable, Father of Monasticism
bio: Born to a wealthy family in Egypt, he sold his possessions to follow Christ's call to the poor and withdrew into the desert, becoming the leader of the Desert Fathers and the model for all later Christian monasticism.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Eastern Desert, Egypt

name: St. Sabbas the Sanctified
title: Venerable
bio: A Cappadocian monastic who settled in the Judean desert and founded the Great Lavra (Mar Saba), composing the Jerusalem Typikon that shaped monastic and liturgical practice across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Monastery and relics — Mar Saba, Judean Desert

name: St. Demetrius of Thessaloniki
title: Great Martyr, Myrrh-streamer
bio: A high-ranking Christian official martyred under Emperor Galerius, he is venerated as the patron and protector of Thessaloniki, where a miraculous flow of fragrant myrrh was later found at his tomb.

locations.label: Place of martyrdom and relics — Thessaloniki

name: St. Paisios of Mount Athos
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: Born Arsenios Eznepidis, his family fled Asia Minor for Greece in his infancy; he became a monk of Mount Athos known for his gentle counsel to the thousands of pilgrims who sought him out, and was canonized in 2015.

locations.label: Death and relics — Souroti, near Thessaloniki

name: St. Gerasimos of Kephalonia
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: Born to a noble Byzantine family, he lived as a hermit on Mount Athos, in Jerusalem, Sinai, Egypt, Crete, and Zakynthos before settling in a cave in Kephalonia, where he restored a church and founded a convent; he is now the island's patron saint.

name: St. Nicholas of Myra
title: Archbishop of Myra, Wonderworker
bio: Bishop of Myra in Lycia and participant in the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, he is venerated throughout the world for his generosity to the poor and his protection of sailors, children, and the falsely accused. His relics were translated to Bari, Italy in 1087.

locations.label: Episcopal see and death — Myra (Demre), Lycia

name: St. John the Baptist
title: Prophet, Forerunner, Baptist
bio: The last of the Old Testament prophets and Forerunner of Christ, he proclaimed repentance in the Judean desert, baptized Jesus in the Jordan, and was martyred by Herod Antipas at the request of Salome. He holds the unique liturgical title “Greater than the prophets.”

locations.label: Baptism of Christ — Qasr al-Yahud, Jordan River

name: St. Athanasios the Great
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who championed Nicene orthodoxy against Arianism throughout his life, enduring five exiles at the hands of Arian emperors. His phrase “Athanasios contra mundum” captures his solitary defense of the full divinity of Christ.

locations.label: Birthplace, episcopal see, and relics — Alexandria

name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
title: Archbishop of Alexandria
bio: Archbishop of Alexandria who presided over the Third Ecumenical Council of Ephesus (431 AD), which confirmed the title Theotokos (“God-bearer”) for the Virgin Mary against the teaching of Nestorius. His prolific theological writings earned him the title “Seal of the Fathers.”

name: St. Makarios of Egypt
title: Venerable, Desert Father
bio: A disciple of St. Anthony the Great who settled in the Scetis desert of Egypt and became one of the most celebrated Desert Fathers, attracting thousands of monks to the Wadi Natrun. He is the reputed author of the Fifty Spiritual Homilies on the life of inner prayer.

locations.label: Monastic life and relics — Wadi el-Natrun (Scetis)

name: St. Seraphim of Sarov
title: Venerable, Wonderworker
bio: A monk of Sarov in Russia who spent years in hermitage and later opened his cell to thousands of pilgrims, greeting each with the words “My joy!” He taught that the aim of the Christian life is the acquisition of the Holy Spirit, and remains one of the most beloved saints of the Russian Church.

locations.label: Monastic life and death — Sarov, Russia

name: St. Porphyrios of Kafsokalyvia
title: Venerable, Elder
bio: A Greek elder who spent decades as a confessor near Athens, renowned for his gift of clairvoyance and his joyful, Christ-centred spiritual direction. He was canonized in 2013 and his collected conversations have been read by millions across the Orthodox world.

locations.label: Priestly ministry and death — Milesi, near Athens
